segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Good morning, North College Library. How can I help you?

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: I was wondering if it was possible to join the library.

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Are you a student at North College?

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: No, I'm not, but someone told me it was possible to join, even if I wasn't.

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: That's right, it is. Are you over 18.? That's our minimum joining age.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Yes, I am.

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: That's no problem then.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Could you tell me what I have to do to join?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Well, you'll need to come in to the library and fill out some forms. You'll also need to bring two passport photos with you. We also need two documents for ID, so a driving licence would be fine.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: I've got that and what else? A credit card?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: No, it needs to have your address on it.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Shall I bring a bank statement, would that do?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: That'll be fine.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Good. Does it cost anything to join?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Well, it's free for students here but otherwise it's £125 per year or £25 if you've got a current student card from another college.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: I was at Westerley College until last year but now I've got a job at Jefferson's steel factory. Er, it's more expensive than I thought. My local library is free.

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: But you'll find they don't have the range of reference books or facilities which we buy for our students. That's why you have to pay to be an external member.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: I see. How many books can I borrow?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: We allow twelve items borrowed at any one time if you're a student, and that includes COs, DVDs and videos. However, it's only eight items for members of the public.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Fine. And how long can I have them for?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Well, you can have both fiction and reference books for four weeks which isn't bad really.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: And what happens if I return them late?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Like all libraries there's a fine system in place. The minimum fine is £1.50 but it can be much higher for some items -up to £5 per week. We'll give you a booklet with all the details when you join. You can always renew items if they're not required by anyone else by telephoning or logging on to our website.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: What about the computers? Can I use them free of charge?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: For college students it's free, but for external members like yourself, the first hour is free and then we make a nominal charge of £I per hour thereafter.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Do I have to book in advance for them?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Oh, yes, it's advisable. Most people tend to book twenty-four hours in advance although sometimes you can get one with only six hours' notice. However, the earliest you can book a computer is forty-eight hours before you need it, and you can only book one hour at a time. If no-one else has booked the computer out, then you may be able to have another hour if you want. We have a wide range of databases, so the computers.are in great demand.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: I'm thinking of doing some writing and I might need to access national newspapers. Do you have them on these databases?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: We do indeed. We've got all the big nationals, The Guardian and The Observer, The Independent and The Times and Sunday Times. We've also got all the local papers and a wide selection of magazines.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Excellent. I assume you have photocopying facilities?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Of course. 5p a sheet for both A4 and A3 black-and-white copies and 40p a sheet for colour. You can get a card from the counter here- it doesn't take coins.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: OK. Oh by the way, another thing I was wondering about was if you ran any writing classes through the library?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: We do, but you'll have to speak to John Grantingham about that. ·He's our resident author. He runs the creative writing classes.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: John .. . Grant . ... Could you spell that for me please?

segments.speaker: LI BRARIAN
segments.en: Certainly. G-R-A-N -T-I-N- G- H-A- M.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Are the classes here at the library?

segments.speaker: LIBRARIAN
segments.en: Yes- he's here on Thursday evenings, oh no sorry, Friday- he's just changed it. You can contact him by emailing the library.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Okay. Right, well that's about all I need to know. Thank you. I'll be along later this week to join. Thanks. Bye.
